Independent code review (8-angle finder pass, medium effort) surfaced 9 candidates, 8 verified real (1 REFUTED — a claimed duplicate of lib/action-link-style.ts's primaryActionLinkStyle, which turned out technically unable to support the :disabled/:focus-visible states real <button> elements need). Most severe: buttons re-enabled via the component's finally block immediately after firing router.refresh() (which returns void and isn't awaited), letting a rushed or double-clicking user fire a since-invalid transition before the refresh had actually landed — fixed by having the component own a local status state, updated in the same batched render as clearing pending, so the rendered button set is never stale relative to whether it's enabled. Also fixed: an unguarded ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS[status] lookup that could throw on an out-of-union status (now falls back to no actions); a silent network-failure catch with no logging (now logs via console.error, closing the same blind-spot class the Project Switcher review already fixed once); a self-contradicting doc comment in page.tsx; a stale claim in dashboard-web-project-detail.md (addended, not rewritten, preserving that document's own historical accuracy); a duplicated .error CSS class (extracted into a new shared error-message.module.css both project-form.module.css and project-status-actions.module.css now compose from); and a duplicated ProjectStatus type alias (now imports the existing ProjectStatusFilter from lib/projects.ts). gates.notes: Cross-domain session-exchange fix for Google SSO login (branch fix-cross-domain-session-exchange, PR #35). Fixes a real production bug: dashboard-api's Google OIDC callback set its session cookie and redirected straight to WEB_APP_ORIGIN's root, but that cookie is host-only to dashboard-api's own *.vercel.app domain (no Domain attribute, no shared parent domain with dashboard-web's separate project) — it was never actually sent on the browser's subsequent navigation to dashboard-web, so every login silently looped back to /auth/sign-in. Not a SameSite bug — SameSite=None is already correct for the cross-site requests this app makes to dashboard-api; the broken case is the browser's own top-level navigation away from it. Fixed with a session-exchange mechanism: a short-lived (60s), single-use, opaque exchange code (migration 00046, session_exchange_codes) redeemed server-to-server against a new POST /auth/exchange endpoint, minting dashboard-web its own independent first-party session (not a relay of the original raw token). Independent code review (high effort, 8-angle finder pass) surfaced 11 candidates, 10 CONFIRMED — most severe: splitting one login into two independent sessions meant 'Sign out' only ever revoked the rarely-used dashboard-api-side session, never the dashboard-web-side one getServerSession() actually authenticates every page against; fixed with a new DELETE /auth/session route in dashboard-web forwarding the whole Cookie header to dashboard-api's /auth/logout with an explicit Origin header. 9 of 10 CONFIRMED findings fixed and re-validated (also: an unguarded exchange-code issue() call that could leak a raw 500 with a session cookie already staged; the active session being stamped with the exchange call's own ipHash/userAgent instead of the real browser's; a missing auth_events record for the session actually in use; an unguarded response.json(); a cookie-name drift risk between the two apps; a hardcoded secure:true with no local-dev override; a duplicated redirect-to-error literal; an extra DB round-trip in redeem()). The 10th (POST /auth/exchange has no OriginCheckGuard/shared secret beyond the code's own entropy/single-use/60s TTL) was left as accepted, tracked debt, flagged explicitly for the second-role reviewer. Security review (run separately, against the fixed branch) found 0 findings above threshold — one candidate (best-effort logout not checking response.ok before clearing the local cookie) was identified and adversarially verified, rejected at 2/10 confidence. gates.notes: /auth/exchange error-masking fix (branch fix-auth-exchange-error-masking, PR #36). Diagnosing a 2026-08-19 sign-in incident (a login racing migration 00046, producing a Postgres 42P01 undefined_table error) surfaced that every failure path in the session-exchange flow -- both GoogleAuthController#callback's sessionExchange.issue() catch block (dashboard-api) and dashboard-web's /auth/exchange route's redirectToAuthError() helper -- redirected to /auth/error?reason=expired regardless of the real failure class, masking a genuine backend error as a routine expired-code case. Fixed by splitting the taxonomy into reason=expired (genuinely expired/invalid: missing OIDC transaction cookie, missing exchange-code param, backend 400) and a new reason=error (everything else). Diagnostics-only -- no change to session cookies, SameSite, OriginCheckGuard, or actual success/failure outcomes, only which message is shown and what gets logged. Independent code review (high effort, 8 finder angles) verified 7 candidates individually: 1 CONFIRMED (REASON_MESSAGES.error duplicating DEFAULT_MESSAGE as a separate literal -- fixed), 5 PLAUSIBLE (shared-type duplication for AuthErrorReason across both apps with no compiler enforcement; a sibling branch in GoogleAuthController#callback that still masks a missing/unparseable OIDC transaction cookie as reason=expired with zero logging; an unguarded body.data destructure that could crash on future API-contract drift, verified not reachable today; the reason=error bucket still collapsing five distinct failure classes into one message; an undocumented, currently-unreachable assumption that a 400 always means expired), 1 REFUTED (dated inline-comment style, verified to match an already-established local convention, dropped). gates.notes: AuthErrorReason shared-type fix (branch fix-auth-error-reason-shared-type, PR #37). Closes one of PR #36's own 5 accepted-debt findings: the /auth/error reason taxonomy (expired/access_denied/error) was declared independently in dashboard-api (bare untyped strings) and dashboard-web (a local type), with no compiler tie between the two independently-deployed apps -- the exact structural shape that let a real backend error get mislabeled expired during the 2026-08-19 production incident. Fixed by promoting a single AuthErrorReason type into packages/shared-types, matching the existing AuthMethod/HealthStatus/SessionRevocationReason precedent -- GoogleAuthController now routes all three redirects through a typed redirectToAuthError() helper; dashboard-web's /auth/exchange route imports the shared type instead of a local copy; /auth/error's REASON_MESSAGES is now typed Record<AuthErrorReason, string> via a new isKnownReason() guard, so the file won't compile if a reason is ever added without a matching message. No behavior change for any real request intended -- a type-safety-only refactor. Independent code review (high effort, 8 finder angles) verified 7 candidates individually: 2 CONFIRMED (isKnownReason() used the `in` operator, which walks the prototype chain, so ?reason=constructor on the public, unauthenticated /auth/error page resolved to an inherited Object.prototype function value instead of a string, crashing the page render -- fixed with Object.hasOwn(); and the unrecognized-reason fallback logged nothing, undercutting the fix's own goal of catching cross-deploy drift between dashboard-api and dashboard-web's independently-deployed Vercel projects -- fixed with a console.error on that path only), 3 PLAUSIBLE (a narrow reason="" behavior change reachable only via a hand-typed URL; a redirectToAuthError name collision between the new dashboard-api controller method and the pre-existing dashboard-web route function; and the incident narrative restated across all 4 changed files' doc comments), 2 REFUTED (widening dashboard-web's route-local AuthErrorReason from 2 values to 3 -- an acceptable, even necessary side effect of the actual fix; and the new redirectToAuthError being a private class method rather than a standalone function -- the more idiomatic NestJS pattern given it needs this.env). Security review (run separately) found 0 findings above threshold -- the one candidate (the new console.error logging the raw, attacker-controlled reason value) was filtered out at confidence 1/10 under the standing 'log spoofing is not a vulnerability' exclusion, since no secondary sink exists and the attacker already knows the value being logged. status=passed/decision=CONFIRM (a clean pass, not an override) because the required second-role human review (Jitesh D, 2026-08-19, decision 'Approved as-is', accepting all 3 open PLAUSIBLE findings as tracked debt, no disputes raised) was already complete before this gate was requested -- see docs/project-state/fix-auth-error-reason-shared-type-approval-checklist.md and its 'Sign-off' section.
